title: seedbank-fewshot-playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is my personal seedbank for few-shot prompt experiments. Goal: collect compact exemplar sets, negative examples, ordering heuristics, and quick failure notes so I can iterate fast when building templates for the prompt library. Not polished — mostly shorthand, TODOs, and results logs.

High-level notes (quick):
- Two axes to explore: exemplar diversity (semantic coverage) vs exemplar closeness (near-neighbor examples). Both affect generalization differently.
- Anchor-first vs anchor-last ordering seems to change bias: anchors early -> model copies style; anchors last -> model rebalances.
- Negative examples are useful for discriminative tasks (e.g., extract/no-extract). Keep explicit "INVALID" label for counterexamples.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Task A: intent-labeling from short chat snippets (binary/multi)
  - Shots tested: 3, 5, 8
  - Variants: homogenous style (all short), diverse style (mix long/short), mixed-domain
  - Observed: 3-shot diverse > 5-shot homogenous on zero-shot generalization to fiddly user phrasing.

- Task B: rewrite-for-tone (casual -> professional)
  - Few-shot template with instruction + 2 examples outperforms single-shot instruction-only at temp 0.0 and 0.2
  - Failure mode: model over-formalizes if exemplars include explicit legalese. Avoid heavy technical exemplars.

Example few-shot templates (copyable):
- Intent extraction (format: JSON {"intent": string})
System: You are a strict extractor. Output only valid JSON with keys: intent, confidence.
1) "Hey, I need to cancel my subscription — how do I do that?" -> {"intent":"cancel_subscription","confidence":"0.95"}
2) "What's the ETA on the new release?" -> {"intent":"product_status","confidence":"0.92"}
3) "I was charged twice for May" -> {"intent":"billing_issue","confidence":"0.98"}
Prompt: "User: \"<USER_TEXT>\" ->"
Notes: include high-confidence numeric strings nudges numeric confidence formatting, model tends to invent decimals if asked for confidence as percent. Better to ask for categorical confidence like 'high/medium/low' if you need stability.

- Rewriting template (style: concise professional)
Instruction: Rewrite the customer message into a concise professional support reply (one paragraph).
EX1: "Ugh my app keeps crashing, please fix it asap" -> "We're sorry you're experiencing crashes. Can you share the app version and steps to reproduce? We'll prioritize this with engineering."
EX2: "I can't get billing to accept my card" -> "Thanks for reporting this. Please confirm the card type and last four digits; we'll investigate the payment gateway logs."
Prompt: "Message: <TEXT>\nRewrite:"

Failure cases observed (real snippets):
- Hallucinated entity: exemplar mentions "account 1847" and model later invents "account 1847 is linked to corporate plan" on unrelated input. Cause: exemplar-specific tokens leak. Mitigation: neutralize or anonymize identifiers in exemplars.
- Instruction drift: when mixing style-change examples and factual transformation examples, model sometimes produces a hybrid (formal but changes facts). Keep tasks single-purpose per prompt.
- Overfitting to punctuation: examples with trailing ellipses cause model to append ellipses in outputs. Normalize punctuation in exemplars.

Negative examples (useful pattern):
- Label: INVALID -> show near-misses to teach what NOT to do. E.g. for entity extraction, include example with partial entity -> label INVALID.
EX: "Transferred cat to John" -> INVALID (ambiguous 'cat' could be a pet or shorthand)
This helps reduce spurious partial matches.

Quick heuristics / checklist for building a new few-shot set:
1) Define single, narrow objective (one-liner).
2) 3-5 exemplars first; increase try by +2 if failing.
3) Make exemplars syntactically varied but semantically consistent.
4) Anonymize long-tail tokens (IDs, URLs).
5) Add 1-2 negative examples for discriminator tasks.
6) Test at temps 0.0 and 0.2; check for hallucination at 0.7.
7) Swap exemplar order: try anchor-first (most prototypical first) and anchor-last.

Quick results log (epoch-like):
- 2026-01-15: Intent labeling 3-shot diverse -> 82% accuracy on dev-set (N=250). Anchor-last performed 3 points better.
- 2026-01-23: Rewriting task 2-shot -> BLEU/ROUGE not useful; human A/B preferred exemplar-based rewrite 68% of time.
- 2026-02-05: Adding 1 INVALID example reduced false positives by ~9% on small test.

Mini debug playbook when prompts fail:
- Re-run with deterministic seed (temp 0.0), confirm reproducible failure.
- Remove latest exemplar; see if failure disappears (to find leaking exemplar).
- Replace any numeric IDs with <ID> placeholder.
- Try instructing "Respond only in JSON" vs structured plain text; JSON enforces parsing but can increase hallucination on missing fields.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Q: How many negative examples is optimal before model learns to be overly conservative? test on recall-sensitive tasks.
- TODO: Run systematic ablation for exemplar-length (short vs long) across 5 tasks. Use Redwood dedicated small-run credits. (Ticket: JIRA-ML-900)
- TODO: add links to stable dataset splits + canonical evaluation harness in prompt-registry.

Useful links / context:
- Slack convo: #prompt-sandbox thread (search "seedbank")
- GH draft: github.com/redwood-inference/prompt-registry/tree/seedbank-experiments (PR 142)
- Related doc: shared_drives/product/prompt-library-guidelines.md (reference style guide)

Notes to self (random):
- Keep 1 saved canonical 3-shot per task that is low-noise and anonymized — use as starting point for PRs.
- For customer-facing templates, add a short "why these exemplars" note in the registry entry.

End of scratchpad.
(Expect to prune and move working bits into prompt-registry entries when stable.)
